title: feat(desktop): import a video into the Library (NIW2-579)
body:
Linear: [NIW2-579](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-579/import-a-video-into-the-library)

## What changed

A video made outside Kaipu (an iPhone `.mov`, a Zoom `.mp4`, a `.webm` from another app) can now be brought into the Library. It becomes a normal recording item, so it plays, opens in the editor, takes tags, and can be exported or prepared for a destination like a Kaipu recording. The "Prepare for…" screen (NIW2-578) is a separate PR. This one only gets outside videos into the Library correctly.

- **Library page:** an **Import a video** button next to the Sync button opens a file dialog (mp4, mov, m4v, webm; several at once). A dashed **Drop a video here — from your phone, Zoom, another app** strip sits under the title. Clicking it opens the same dialog.
- **Drag and drop:** while the Library is open, video files dropped **anywhere in the window** are imported, and the strip lights up during the drag. Files that are not videos are skipped, and a toast names them.
- **Feedback:** if exactly one video comes in, a toast offers **Open** (its page). Several show a count. A failure names the file and the reason ("it has no video in it", "Kaipu can't read this video", …). The other files in the batch still import.
- **Marker:** imported items show **Imported** in the card and row metadata line, and **IMPORTED** in the detail page metadata, where Kaipu recordings show SCREEN / FRAME / WINDOW.
- **i18n:** every string is in `en.json` and `es.json`. That includes the main-process dialog title, button and file-type label (`dialogs.importVideo*`).
- **Docs:** `backlog/import-video` (🟢 Ready to validate), with a backlog index row and a sidebar entry.

## Decisions

**How an imported item is represented.** It uses the same layout `RecordingWriter.finalize` leaves, so there is no parallel format:
- `<vault>/imported-<timestamp>[-n].<ext>` holds a **copy** of the source.
- `.kaipu/<id>.json` holds the sidecar: `title` = the source file name without its extension, `durationSeconds`, `createdAt` = the import time, `derivedFromAssetId: null`, and **`capture: { mode: "import", width, height, ratio: null }`**.

I put the import marker in `capture` and did not add a new `origin` field. `capture` is already the field that says where a take came from, and it already carries the video size, which the Prepare screen will want for any source. Builds that predate the new mode read the value as `null` (`sanitizeRecordingCapture`) and list the item as a plain recording. No migration is needed, and every older item stays valid.

**The container is kept** (`.mov` stays `.mov`, with the extension lowercased). The vault bytes are exactly the bytes the user picked. `LibraryVault` now also lists `.mov` and `.m4v`. The media protocol already serves `.webm` as `application/octet-stream`, and `.mov`/`.m4v` take the same path.

**Validation happens in main, with what the app already has (no ffmpeg, no new dependency).** mediabunny is already a dependency, and it demuxes files in Node through `FilePathSource`. Main never trusts a renderer path:
1. The payload must be a list of strings, at most 50.
2. Each path must be absolute, have an importable extension, exist, be a regular readable file, and **not already be inside the vault**. A Library card dragged out and dropped back would otherwise be imported twice.
3. The file is copied (an APFS clone where the volume supports it) to a staged `<vault>/import.<ext>.<pid>.<uuid>.part` and fsynced. `.part` files are never listed.
4. The **copy** is probed: it must parse, have a video track with a known codec, and have a duration. Audio-only and non-media files are refused.
5. Under a per-vault lock, a free id is picked. It is never the id of an existing file, or of a sidecar left behind by "remove local copy". The sidecar is written, then the copy is renamed in.
6. Any failure removes the staged copy, plus the sidecar and media if they were written. **Nothing half-imported remains.** The source is only ever read (ADR 0003).

**Poster and hash reuse the existing paths.** Main has no video decoder. The Library's orphan heal (`useOrphanHeal` → `backfillLocalRecordingMeta`) already makes the poster for any recording without one, in the renderer through WebCodecs. The content hash stays lazy (`ensureContentHash`), as it is for recordings.

**The drop target is the whole window while the Library is mounted,** not just the page `div`. Electron's default for an unhandled file drop is to navigate the window to the file, so dropping a video just beside a short list would otherwise unload the app.

## Limits (also in the doc)

- Main checks that a video **demuxes**, not that it **decodes** on this machine. If WebCodecs can't decode a codec, the video still imports, but it gets no poster and fails in the editor. I have not checked this on real iPhone HEVC or Zoom files. The steps below cover it.
- An import has no progress bar or cancel. A multi-GB copy keeps the button on "Importing…" until it finishes.
- `createdAt` is the import time, not the time the video was shot.
- Dropping a file while **another** page is open still triggers Electron's default navigation. That behavior predates this PR and is unchanged here.

## Verification

- `bun run verify` from the repo root: green (kaipu-record: 312 files, 2,992 tests).
- New tests:
  - `import-video.test.ts`: validation, atomic copy and cleanup on probe failure, probe throw, unwritable vault, id clashes, no reuse of a cloud-only id, refusing vault files, the batch cap, and a real MP4 through the default probe.
  - Renderer tests for the button, drop zone and window drop handling, the toasts, and the Imported marker on the card, row and detail page.
  - Recording-capture tests for the new mode.
- `electron-vite build`, with a placeholder `MAIN_VITE_SERVER_URL`, bundles the import code. Main loads `mediabunny` through `require`, and I checked that require path in plain Node against the fixture.
- **Not run in Electron.** Runtime QA is the owner's.

## How to test it yourself

1. Build or run this branch, and open **Library**. Next to the title there is an **Import a video** button, and under it a dashed "Drop a video here — from your phone, Zoom, another app" strip.
2. Click **Import a video** and pick an **iPhone `.mov`** (HEVC if you have one). Expected: a toast says "“IMG_xxxx” is in your Library" with **Open**. The card appears at the top with a poster after a moment, and its metadata line ends in "· Imported".
3. Click **Open** in that toast, or click the card. Expected: the detail page metadata shows **IMPORTED**, the video plays, and **Edit** opens it in the editor.
4. Import a **Zoom `.mp4`** by clicking the dashed strip. Expected: same result as step 2.
5. Import a **`.webm`**. Expected: same result.
6. Import a **non-video file** that you renamed to `.mp4` (for example a `.txt` renamed to `notes.mp4`). Expected: an error toast "Couldn’t import notes.mp4: Kaipu can’t read this video". Nothing new appears in the Library, and no `import*.part` file is left in the recordings folder (Settings → open the recordings folder).
7. **Drag and drop:** drag two videos and a `.pdf` from Finder onto the Library window, including onto the sidebar. Expected: the strip lights up ("Drop to import into your Library") while you drag. On drop, a toast says "2 videos imported" and another says the `.pdf` was skipped.
8. Drag a Library card out (to the desktop or Finder) and drop it back onto the Library. Expected: "Couldn’t import …: it’s already in your Library", and no duplicate appears.
9. Check that **the originals are untouched**: in Finder, each source file from steps 2–5 is still in place with the same size and modified date. The recordings folder holds copies named `imported-<date>.<ext>`.
10. Switch the app language to Español and repeat step 2. Expected: the button, strip, toasts and the native file dialog title read in Spanish ("Importar un video", "IMPORTADO").
